facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old man presented with a painful nodule on the lower part of his right leg
the lesion had been stable in size and painless for 4 years but had enlarged and become tender over the past 6 months
an irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm was noted just above the lateral malleolus of the right leg
No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy was present
there were no other suspicious cutaneous lesions
Routine blood tests, including complete blood count, fasting blood sugar, liver and renal function tests, were within normal limits
Tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV were negative
a lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass partly covered by skin, measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm
nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma
Mitotic figures, including atypical forms, measured 7–8 per 10 high-power fields
Immunohistochemical staining showed strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45
The tumor cells were negative for S-100 protein, pancytokeratin, epithelial membrane antigen, and CD31

rationales.F02: The lesion's recent growth and tenderness suggest a possible malignant transformation, which is more typical of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans or leiomyosarcoma than malignant melanoma.
rationales.F09: The presence of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma is highly suggestive of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans or leiomyosarcoma.
rationales.F10: The high mitotic rate, including atypical forms, is more typical of malignant tumors such as dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans or leiomyosarcoma.
rationales.F11: The strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45 suggest a possible melanocytic origin, but the absence of other melanoma-specific features makes malignant melanoma less likely.
rationales.F12: The negative staining for S-100 protein, pancytokeratin, epithelial membrane antigen, and CD31 helps to rule out other tumor types, including malignant melanoma, and supports the diagnosis of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma, along with immunohistochemical staining showing strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45, decided it.
